dimension: Database schema, migrations, constraints, integrity (data/signaldeck.db, daemon/internal/store)
title: prediction_ledger has no uniqueness on its identity key: 335 bars carry two conflicting frozen pre-registrations, 15 of them disagreeing on the published probability
symptom: The append-only hash-chained ledger, which the platform publishes as the tamper-evident record of what was predicted for a given bar, contains two entries for the same (symbol_id, horizon, bar_ts) in 335 cases. 15 of those pairs carry two different cal_prob values and 124 carry two different feature_hash values, so for those bars the ledger does not answer "what was frozen for this bar" with one value.
evidence:
python (mode=ro) on data/signaldeck.db:
  dup identity groups: 335
  groups with DIFFERING cal_prob: 15
  groups with DIFFERING feature_hash: 124

Example group (symbol_id=1, horizon='1d', bar_ts=1783751520):
  seq 30716  predicted_at 1783751525  raw 0.5876438861751181  cal 0.7231182795698925  fh 0820e819e3c0...
  seq 30780  predicted_at 1783751740  raw 0.5660684528515558  cal 0.7188328912466844  fh a153d72f6d59...
  predictions row: (1783751520, 0.5660684528515558, 0.7188328912466844, 1)   <- only the LATER value survives
  features rows for that key: [(id 34519, version 3, len(vec) 548)]          <- only ONE vector survives

DDL confirms no unique key on the identity:
  CREATE TABLE prediction_ledger ( seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, ... )
  IDX idx_prediction_ledger_ident | CREATE INDEX idx_prediction_ledger_ident ON prediction_ledger (symbol_id, horizon, bar_ts)   <- NON-unique

GET /api/ledger/verify -> {"count":483425,"intact":true,...} — the chain hash check cannot detect this class, because both rows were validly appended.

Date range of the affected bars: 2026-07-10T05:01:00Z .. 2026-08-04T20:41:00Z (ledger itself spans 2026-07-04 .. 2026-09-10).
root_cause: pipeline/predict.go writes the prediction with UpsertPrediction (INSERT OR REPLACE, store/predict.go:69) and the feature vector with InsertFeatures (ON CONFLICT(symbol_id,horizon,ts,version) DO UPDATE SET vec=excluded.vec, features.go:44) — both overwrite in place — and then calls AppendLedger, which unconditionally APPENDS (ledger.go:141, "Never updates or replaces an existing row") with no freeze-once check and no unique constraint behind it. When the predictor runs a second pass against the same still-current bar, the prediction and the feature vector are replaced while the ledger gains a second, contradictory entry. Because features is keyed (symbol_id, horizon, ts, version) and only one row survives, at most one of the two recorded feature_hash values can still be recomputed from persisted data — the other 124 entries reference a vector that no longer exists.
user_impact: For 335 bars the published pre-registration record is ambiguous, and for 124 of them a ledger entry's feature_hash cannot be reproduced from any persisted feature vector — i.e. those forecasts cannot be traced back to their inputs, which is exactly the release-critical class. The occurrences stopped after 2026-08-04, but nothing in the schema or the write path prevents recurrence.
proposed_fix: Make freeze-once structural rather than behavioural: add CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON prediction_ledger (symbol_id, horizon, bar_ts) (after reconciling the 335 existing groups — supersede the loser the way regime_outcomes does with superseded_by, do not delete), and have AppendLedger return the existing entry instead of appending when one already exists for that identity. If a re-emit is legitimately a new belief, it needs its own supersede marker and the features row needs a version bump so the superseded hash stays reproducible.
repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/signaldeck.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute('select count(*) from (select symbol_id,horizon,bar_ts from prediction_ledger group by 1,2,3 having count(*)>1 and count(distinct cal_prob)>1)').fetchone())"

dimension: Database schema, migrations, constraints, integrity (data/signaldeck.db, daemon/internal/store)
title: The prediction write is four separate transactions, so a crash mid-write leaves a served forecast with no ledger entry and no dq record — 29 such rows exist, 28 of them silent
symptom: 29 served predictions (n_used>0) written since the ledger began have no matching prediction_ledger row, so they were published without the pre-registration entry the platform claims covers every prediction. Only one ledger_append_error dq event exists, so 28 of them left no trace at all.
evidence:
python (mode=ro):
  served predictions with NO ledger entry (whole ledger era): 29
  served total: 480202
  ledger_append_error dq events: 1

(The raw gap is 55,352 of 538,400, but 55,323 of those are n_used=0 EVIDENCE rows that are deliberately never ledgered — see predict_evidence.go:16. Excluding them leaves 29.)

worker_runs shows the daemon does die mid-run:
  2026-09-10T04:23:09Z orphaned | process died mid-run; swept at boot 1789014209
root_cause: UpsertPrediction (its own tx, store/predict.go:63), SeedBenchmarkOutcome, InsertFeatures and AppendLedger (its own tx, ledger.go:141) are four independent transactions on the single writer. The prediction commits first and the ledger append is explicitly best-effort ("a ledger failure logs + records a dq event but MUST NOT fail the prediction"). A process death between the two commits produces a durable prediction with no chain entry, and the dq event that would have recorded the miss is itself in the process that died.
user_impact: 0.006% of served forecasts are outside the tamper-evident chain, and nothing in the system reports which ones. The published claim that every prediction is pre-registered is very nearly true but not exactly true, and there is no surface that says so.
proposed_fix: Either wrap the prediction + outcome-seed + feature + ledger writes in ONE transaction on the writer (they already share s.w, so this costs nothing in concurrency), or add a startup/periodic reconciler that reports predictions with n_used>0 and no ledger row as a dq event so the gap is counted rather than invisible.

title: Every resolved-side read of score_outcomes full-scans 6.75M rows; the equivalent index exists on prediction_outcomes but not here
symptom: score_outcomes is the largest non-bar table at 6,752,825 rows and carries only one secondary index — idx_outcomes_unresolved, a partial index on resolved_at IS NULL. The honesty-page reads filter on resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND horizon=?, which that index cannot serve, so both queries scan the whole table.
evidence:
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on the production query text from store.go:1214 (ResolvedOutcomes):
  SCAN score_outcomes
  USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on the unresolved queue:
  SEARCH score_outcomes USING INDEX idx_outcomes_unresolved (resolved_at=?)
Measured warm on the live file (mode=ro):
  ResolvedOutcomes 1d limit 5000 -> 5000 rows in 0.5s
  ResolvedOutcomesIndependent-shaped window query (1d) -> 18,882 groups in 1.4s
The sibling table has exactly the missing index:
  idx_predoutcomes_resolved_hts | CREATE INDEX ... ON prediction_outcomes (horizon, ts DESC) WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND up IS NOT NULL
  -> EXPLAIN on the prediction_outcomes resolved read: SEARCH prediction_outcomes USING INDEX idx_predoutcomes_resolved_hts (horizon=?)
root_cause: The resolved-side partial index was added for prediction_outcomes when that read path was optimised and never mirrored onto score_outcomes, which has 9x the rows.
user_impact: Warm single-query latency is acceptable (0.5–1.4s), so this is not a blocker. But it is a full scan of the biggest table on a public read path served by a 4-connection pool, it grows with the table, and a long scan is exactly the reader that starves the WAL TRUNCATE checkpoint the storage governor documents at store.go:66-88. I measured warm cache only; cold and under concurrent load will be worse and I did not measure that.
proposed_fix: Mirror the existing index: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_score_outcomes_resolved_hts ON score_outcomes (horizon, ts DESC) WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL. One line in schema.sql, same shape as the prediction_outcomes one that is already proven to be chosen by the planner.

  id=805 notional= 78.2276 cost=0.027380 -> 3.5000 bps

symptom: paperOrder converts the requested quantity to `budget = qty * bar.Open` and hands it to EnterLong, which solves N*(1+spread+impact)=budget. The filled quantity is therefore always strictly less than the requested quantity, by the whole execution cost.

paperorder.go:108 `fill, gotQty, _, okFill = papertrade.EnterLong(budget, in)`

title: Collapsed cross-sections are caused by the CALIBRATION layer, not by features, a clamp, or a market-wide signal
symptom: The publication gate refuses on days like "1d 2026-08-06 (33 distinct across 327 symbols)". The gate message says the universe "receives a handful of distinct probabilities", which reads as a broken feature pipeline or a constant. It is not: the RAW ensemble cross-section on every one of those days is well dispersed, and only the calibrated output is degenerate.
evidence:
Deduped to one row per symbol per day (the gate's own unit), horizon 1d:
  2026-08-06: 329 symbols, raw 159 distinct@3dp, raw range 0.6474 (0.30177→0.94920) → calibrated 33 distinct@3dp, cal range 0.0562 (0.46387→0.52006)
  2026-07-27: raw 187 distinct, range 0.8477 → cal 6 distinct, range 0.0100
  2026-07-31: raw 183 → cal 6;  2026-08-03: raw 186 → cal 6;  2026-08-04: raw 188 → cal 13
And for the gate firing RIGHT NOW (it measures the prior published day, 2026-09-08, horizon 1d, 329 symbols):
  raw p95−p05 = 0.2287  |  calibrated p95−p05 = 0.0174   (floor = MinCrossSectionSpread 0.05)
That is a ~13x compression introduced entirely between raw_prob and cal_prob.
root_cause: Both calibration tiers are isotonic (PAV) fits of raw_prob against realized `up`. Because the directional record carries almost no information (settled verdict: directional IC ~0.02), PAV pools nearly the whole raw range into 1-3 blocks, so the map degenerates to a near-constant equal to the base rate. globalCalibration (predict.go:135) already mitigates this with ensemble.CalibrateRanking (beta.go:281), which keeps a ranking-preserving map unless isotonic is significantly better out of sample. The per-symbol tier does NOT: symbolagent uses ensemble.CalibrateKnots (ensemble.go:952), plain PAV with no ranking-preservation and no out-of-sample Brier gate. The gate then correctly refuses the compressed output, so the visible symptom is a publication refusal whose stated cause ("a handful of distinct probabilities") names the effect, not the mechanism.
user_impact: The refusal text points a reader at the wrong layer, so the recorded diagnosis across audits/registry/README is "the model stopped discriminating" when the model's own cross-section is fine and the recalibration step is destroying it. Any remediation aimed at features or leg admission cannot clear the gate. On publication days it also means the served probability carries far less symbol-specific information than the ensemble computed.
proposed_fix: Apply the CalibrateRanking contract to the per-symbol tier too (accept an isotonic map only when it beats the ranking-preserving map out of sample on a day-clustered split), and refuse any map whose fitted output spread is below MinCrossSectionSpread at fit time rather than discovering it a day later at the gate. Separately, amend the gate's reason string to state the measured raw spread beside the calibrated spread, so the refusal names the layer that collapsed.
